subproblems.title: Unweighted monotonicity identity: the case h ≡ 1 of the weighted identity (parent Step 1)
subproblems.statement: Let (WMI) be the frozen statement of the sibling weighted_monotonicity_identity: for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, every rectifiable n-varifold V in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with weight μ_V, every U ⊆ E, H: E → E, h: E → ℝ, ξ ∈ E and σ, ρ ∈ ℝ, if n > 0, μ_V is finite on compact sets, dim T_xV = n for μ_V-a.e. x, x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable, U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H in U, h is C¹ on U, tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U and 0 < σ ≤ ρ, then (a) τ ↦ τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩dμ_V is integrable on (σ, ρ], (b) x ↦ h(x)q_ξ(x)/|x−ξ|ⁿ is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ), and (c) ρ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ(ξ)}h dμ_V − σ^{-n}∫_{B_σ(ξ)}h dμ_V = ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} h q_ξ/|x−ξ|ⁿ dμ_V + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h + hH⟩dμ_V dτ. Let (GF) be: for every n > 0, ℓ and every V, μ_V is finite on compact sets, dim T_xV = n for μ_V-a.e. x, and x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable. Then (WMI) and (GF) imply (UI): for all n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H such that V has generalized mean curvature H in U, ξ, and 0 < σ ≤ ρ with B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U: (i) e(τ) := τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩dμ_V is integrable on (σ, ρ]; (ii) w_ξ(x) := q_ξ(x)/|x−ξ|ⁿ is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ); (iii) ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ(ξ)) − σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ(ξ)) = ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} w_ξ dμ_V + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e(τ)dτ. Here B_t(ξ) is the closed ball, q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x, μ_V(B) is the real number V.weight.real B, and all integrals are Bochner integrals.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; μ_V = V.weight; B_t(ξ) = closedBall ξ t; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x; w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x−ξ|ⁿ; ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_{T_xV}(∇h(x)) with p_{T_xV} = (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection; μ_V(B) means V.weight.real B; all integrals are Bochner integrals. (WMI) and (GF) are the two antecedents displayed in the statement.
1. Assume (WMI) and (GF). Fix n, ℓ, V, U, H, ξ, σ, ρ with 0 < n, U open, V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, 0 < σ and σ ≤ ρ. Applying (GF) to (n, ℓ, V) and 0 < n gives (FV1) μ_V is finite on compact sets, (FV2) dim T_xV = n for μ_V-a.e. x, (FV3) x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable.
2. Let h: E → ℝ be the constant function h(x) = 1. A constant function is C¹, so h is C¹ on U. Its support {h ≠ 0} is all of E, hence tsupport h = closure(E) = E and tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) = B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U.
3. By 1 and 2 every hypothesis of (WMI) holds for (n, ℓ, V, U, H, h, ξ, σ, ρ). Hence (a) τ ↦ τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩dμ_V is integrable on (σ, ρ]; (b) x ↦ h(x)w_ξ(x) is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ); (c) ρ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ(ξ)}h dμ_V − σ^{-n}∫_{B_σ(ξ)}h dμ_V = ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} h(x)w_ξ(x)dμ_V + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩dμ_V dτ.
4. Pointwise simplifications. The gradient of the constant function h vanishes at every point, so ∇^M h(x) = p_{T_xV}(0) = 0 because p_{T_xV} is linear. Also h(x)H(x) = 1·H(x) = H(x). Hence ⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩ = ⟨x−ξ, 0 + H(x)⟩ = ⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩ for every x, so for every τ the τ-integrand in (a) and (c) equals e(τ) = τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩dμ_V. Further h(x)w_ξ(x) = w_ξ(x), and for t ∈ {σ, ρ}, ∫_{B_t(ξ)}h dμ_V = ∫_{B_t(ξ)}1 dμ_V = V.weight.real(B_t(ξ))·1 (the integral of a constant over a set is the real measure of the set times the constant).
5. Substituting 4 into (a), (b), (c) gives exactly (i) e is integrable on (σ, ρ], (ii) w_ξ is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ), and (iii) ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ(ξ)) − σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ(ξ)) = ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} w_ξ dμ_V + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e(τ)dτ. Since n, ℓ, V, U, H, ξ, σ, ρ were arbitrary, (UI) holds. ∎

h ≡ 1 is C¹ on U and tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) = B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U
Apply (WMI) to (n, ℓ, V, U, H, h ≡ 1, ξ, σ, ρ)
Simplify pointwise: ∇^M 1 = p_{T_xV}(0) = 0, 1·H = H, 1·w_ξ = w_ξ, ∫_{B_t}1 dμ_V = μ_V(B_t)

subproblems.title: Integration by parts of the annular monotonicity identity against an absolutely continuous factor (parent Step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets, ξ ∈ E, w: E → ℝ with w(x) ≥ 0 for all x, a, e, F, F': ℝ → ℝ, and 0 < σ ≤ ρ. Write B_t for the closed ball of radius t about ξ and A := B_ρ∖B_σ. Assume: w is μ-integrable on A; e is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ]; a(t) − a(s) = ∫_{B_t∖B_s} w dμ + ∫_{(s,t]} e(τ)dτ for all σ ≤ s ≤ t ≤ ρ; F' is integrable on (σ, ρ]; and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]} F'(τ)dτ for every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Then x ↦ F(|x−ξ|)w(x) is μ-integrable on A, and F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = ∫_A F(|x−ξ|)w(x)dμ(x) + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} (F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ))dτ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (w : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (a e F F' : ℝ → ℝ) (σ ρ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ w x) → IntegrableOn w (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) μ → IntegrableOn e (Ioc σ ρ) → (∀ s t : ℝ, σ ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ ρ → a t - a s = ∫ x in closedBall ξ t \ closedBall ξ s, w x ∂μ + ∫ τ in Ioc s t, e τ) → IntegrableOn F' (Ioc σ ρ) → (∀ t ∈ Icc σ ρ, F t = F σ + ∫ τ in Ioc σ t, F' τ) → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ F ‖x - ξ‖ * w x) (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) μ ∧ F ρ * a ρ - F σ * a σ = ∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ, F ‖x - ξ‖ * w x ∂μ + ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, (F τ * e τ + F' τ * a τ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
0. Notation. r(x) := |x−ξ| = dist(x, ξ), so B_t = {x : r(x) ≤ t}. For σ ≤ t ≤ ρ we have B_ρ∖B_t = {x ∈ A : t < r(x)} (if r(x) > t ≥ σ then x ∉ B_σ); in particular A = {x : σ < r(x) ≤ ρ}. μ(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ) < ∞ because B_ρ is compact, so μ⌞A is a finite measure; λ denotes Lebesgue measure and all integrals over (s, t] are λ-integrals. Put W := ∫_A w dμ ∈ [0, ∞) and ‖e‖ := ∫_{(σ,ρ]}|e|.
1. For t ∈ [σ, ρ] let D(t) := ∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ and P(t) := ∫_{(t,ρ]} e. Since w ≥ 0 is integrable on A and B_ρ∖B_t ⊆ A decreases as t increases, D is nonincreasing on [σ, ρ] with 0 ≤ D ≤ W = D(σ). P is continuous on [σ, ρ] (absolute continuity of the integral) and |P| ≤ ‖e‖.
2. The hypothesis with (s, t) := (t, ρ) gives a(t) = a(ρ) − D(t) − P(t) for every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Hence on [σ, ρ], a is Borel measurable (a constant plus a monotone function plus a continuous function) and bounded: |a| ≤ M_a := |a(ρ)| + W + ‖e‖.
3. From F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}F' on [σ, ρ], F is continuous on [σ, ρ] (indefinite integral of an integrable function), hence bounded there: |F| ≤ M_F := |F(σ)| + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}|F'|.
4. Integrability. (a) r maps A continuously into (σ, ρ] ⊆ [σ, ρ], and F is continuous on [σ, ρ]; so F∘r is continuous on the Borel set A, hence μ⌞A-measurable, and |F(r(x))w(x)| ≤ M_F w(x). Thus F(r)w is μ-integrable on A, which is the first assertion. (b) F·e, F'·a, F'·D and F'·P are integrable on (σ, ρ]: each is the product of an integrable function (e or F') with a function that is bounded and measurable on [σ, ρ] (by 1–3).
5. Write F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) + (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ).
6. The hypothesis with (s, t) := (σ, ρ) gives F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) = F(σ)W + F(σ)∫_{(σ,ρ]}e.
7. The hypothesis on F at t = ρ and step 2 (a(ρ) = a(t) + D(t) + P(t) for t ∈ (σ, ρ]) give (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ) = ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'(t)a(ρ)dt = ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'a + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'D + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'P, all three integrable by 4(b).
8. Fubini on the annulus. Let Φ(t, x) := F'(t)w(x)1{t < r(x)} on (σ, ρ] × A with the finite product measure λ⌞(σ,ρ] ⊗ μ⌞A. Φ is measurable (F' and w are a.e.-strongly measurable and {(t, x) : t < r(x)} is open) and ∫∫|Φ| ≤ (∫_{(σ,ρ]}|F'|)·W < ∞, so Fubini's theorem applies. For fixed t ∈ (σ, ρ], ∫_A w(x)1{t < r(x)}dμ(x) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ = D(t) by 0. For fixed x ∈ A, {t ∈ (σ, ρ] : t < r(x)} = (σ, r(x)), which differs from (σ, r(x)] by one point, so ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'(t)1{t < r(x)}dt = ∫_{(σ,r(x)]}F' = F(r(x)) − F(σ) by the hypothesis on F at t = r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ]. Therefore ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'(t)D(t)dt = ∫_A w(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ))dμ(x) = ∫_A F(r)w dμ − F(σ)W.
9. Fubini on the triangle. Let Ψ(t, s) := F'(t)e(s)1{t < s} on (σ, ρ]² with λ ⊗ λ; Ψ is measurable and ∫∫|Ψ| ≤ (∫|F'|)·‖e‖ < ∞. For fixed t, ∫_{(σ,ρ]}e(s)1{t < s}ds = P(t); for fixed s ∈ (σ, ρ], ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'(t)1{t < s}dt = ∫_{(σ,s)}F' = ∫_{(σ,s]}F' = F(s) − F(σ). By Fubini, ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F'(t)P(t)dt = ∫_{(σ,ρ]}e(s)(F(s) − F(σ))ds = ∫_{(σ,ρ]}Fe − F(σ)∫_{(σ,ρ]}e.
10. Adding 6, 7, 8, 9 (linearity is justified by 4): F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = F(σ)W + F(σ)∫e + ∫F'a + (∫_A F(r)w dμ − F(σ)W) + (∫Fe − F(σ)∫e) = ∫_A F(|x−ξ|)w(x)dμ(x) + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}(F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ))dτ, since the terms containing F(σ) cancel. ∎

a = a(ρ) − D − P on [σ, ρ] with D monotone and P continuous, so a is bounded Borel; F is continuous hence bounded on [σ, ρ]

This is the absolute-continuity claim used in Steps 3 and 5 of the parent proof ('Φ(t) := ∫_{(0,t]}E is Lipschitz with Φ' = E a.e., so F = exp(−Φ) is absolutely continuous with F' = −EF a.e.'; '(5.3) Φ_0 is absolutely continuous with Φ_0' = F_0 a.e., so F = exp(−Φ_0) is absolutely continuous with F' = −F_0F a.e.'), for a general integrable g.
1. If R ≤ 0 then (0, R] = ∅, so the integrability claim is trivial, and 0 ≤ σ ≤ t ≤ R forces σ = t = R = 0, where the identity reads F(0) = F(0) + 0. Assume R > 0.
2. For τ ∈ [0, R], (0, τ] ⊆ (0, R], so Φ(τ) := ∫_{(0,τ]}g = ∫_0^τ g is defined, |Φ(τ)| ≤ M := ∫_{(0,R]}|g|, and Φ is continuous on [0, R] (dominated convergence: g·1_{(0,τ]} is dominated by |g|·1_{(0,R]}). Hence F = exp(−Φ) is continuous on [0, R] with 0 < F ≤ e^M there.
3. Integrability: g·F is a.e.-strongly measurable on (0, R] (an integrable function times a function continuous on [0, R]) and |g(τ)F(τ)| ≤ e^M|g(τ)|, so −gF is integrable on (0, R]. This is the first assertion.
4. Φ is absolutely continuous on [0, R] (an indefinite integral of an integrable function), and by the Lebesgue differentiation theorem, for a.e. τ ∈ (0, R), Φ is differentiable at τ with Φ'(τ) = g(τ).
5. exp is Lipschitz on [−M, M] with constant e^M and Φ([0, R]) ⊆ [−M, M]; a Lipschitz function composed with an absolutely continuous function is absolutely continuous, so F = exp∘(−Φ) is absolutely continuous on [0, R]. At each τ as in 4, the chain rule gives that F is differentiable at τ with F'(τ) = −Φ'(τ)exp(−Φ(τ)) = −g(τ)F(τ). So the a.e. derivative of F equals −gF a.e. on (0, R).
6. Fundamental theorem of calculus for absolutely continuous functions: for 0 ≤ σ ≤ t ≤ R, F is absolutely continuous on [σ, t], so F(t) − F(σ) = ∫_σ^t F'(τ)dτ with F' the a.e. derivative. By 5, F' = −gF a.e. on (σ, t), and since σ ≤ t the interval integral equals the integral over (σ, t]. Hence F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}(−g(τ)F(τ))dτ. ∎

For η ∈ E and ρ > 0 write a_η(ρ) := μ(B_ρ(η))/ρⁿ (closed balls, real-valued measure). Suppose that for every ξ ∈ U there exist r > 0 and c: ℝ → ℝ with c(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 such that for every η with |η − ξ| < r there are F, E: ℝ → ℝ with e^{−c(ρ)} ≤ F(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)} and |E(ρ)| ≤ c(ρ) for all ρ ∈ (0, r), and with ρ ↦ F(ρ)a_η(ρ) + E(ρ) nondecreasing on (0, r). This lemma isolates the density argument shared by the parent proof's Step 3 (remark after 3.17: 'ρ ↦ F(ρ)a(ρ) is nondecreasing ... so it has a limit L; since F(ρ) → 1, a(ρ) → L ... upper semicontinuity ... continuity from above') and Step 6 (4.9: 'Ψ = Fa + F − 1 is nondecreasing ... Ψ(ρ) → L; since F(ρ) → 1, a(ρ) → L ... uniform Λ near ξ ... continuity from above').
0. Preliminaries. ω := ω_n = omega n > 0: the open unit ball of ℝⁿ is nonempty and open, so its Lebesgue measure is positive, and bounded, so finite; ω is that measure. For η ∈ E and ρ > 0, B_ρ(η) is compact, so μ(B_ρ(η)) < ∞, a_η(ρ) ≥ 0, and μ(B_ρ(η))/(ωρⁿ) = a_η(ρ)/ω.
1. Key claim. Let ξ ∈ U with data r, c as in the hypothesis, let |η − ξ| < r, and let F, E be the functions provided for η; put Ψ(ρ) := F(ρ)a_η(ρ) + E(ρ) for ρ ∈ (0, r). Then: (a) L_η := lim_{ρ↓0}Ψ(ρ) exists in ℝ and L_η ≤ Ψ(ρ) for every ρ ∈ (0, r); (b) a_η(ρ) → L_η as ρ ↓ 0; (c) V.HasDensityAt η (V.density η) and ω·V.density η = L_η; (d) ω·V.density η ≤ e^{c(ρ)}a_η(ρ) + c(ρ) for every ρ ∈ (0, r).
Proof of (a): on (0, r), c(ρ) ≥ |E(ρ)| ≥ 0. Since c(ρ) → 0, fix ρ₀ ∈ (0, r) with c ≤ 1 on (0, ρ₀]. For ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀], Ψ(ρ) ≥ E(ρ) ≥ −c(ρ) ≥ −1 because F(ρ) ≥ e^{−c(ρ)} > 0 and a_η(ρ) ≥ 0; for ρ ∈ [ρ₀, r), Ψ(ρ) ≥ Ψ(ρ₀) ≥ −1 by monotonicity. A nondecreasing function on (0, r) that is bounded below converges as ρ ↓ 0 to its infimum L_η := inf_{(0,r)}Ψ ∈ [−1, ∞), and L_η ≤ Ψ(ρ) for all ρ ∈ (0, r).
Proof of (b): e^{−c(ρ)} ≤ F(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)} and c(ρ) → 0 give F(ρ) → e⁰ = 1 by squeezing and continuity of exp; |E(ρ)| ≤ c(ρ) gives E(ρ) → 0. As F(ρ) > 0, a_η(ρ) = (Ψ(ρ) − E(ρ))/F(ρ) → (L_η − 0)/1 = L_η.
Proof of (c): by 0 and (b), μ(B_ρ(η))/(ωρⁿ) = a_η(ρ)/ω → L_η/ω as ρ ↓ 0, i.e. V.HasDensityAt η (L_η/ω). The filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 in (0, ∞) is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff, so V.density η, defined as the limUnder of this quotient along that filter, equals L_η/ω. Hence V.HasDensityAt η (V.density η) and ω·V.density η = L_η.
Proof of (d): for ρ ∈ (0, r), L_η ≤ Ψ(ρ) = F(ρ)a_η(ρ) + E(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)}a_η(ρ) + c(ρ), using F(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)}, a_η(ρ) ≥ 0 and E(ρ) ≤ |E(ρ)| ≤ c(ρ).
2. Existence. For ξ ∈ U apply 1(c) with η := ξ (|ξ − ξ| = 0 < r). So V.HasDensityAt ξ (V.density ξ) for every ξ ∈ U.
3. Upper semicontinuity. Fix ξ ∈ U with data r, c, and t > V.density ξ. By 1(b),(c) with η = ξ, a_ξ(ρ) → ω·V.density ξ, hence e^{c(ρ)}a_ξ(ρ) + c(ρ) → ω·V.density ξ < ωt as ρ ↓ 0; choose ρ ∈ (0, r) with e^{c(ρ)}a_ξ(ρ) + c(ρ) < ωt. The closed balls B_{ρ+δ}(ξ) decrease as δ ↓ 0 with intersection B_ρ(ξ) and μ(B_{ρ+1}(ξ)) < ∞, so by continuity of measure from above μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ)) → μ(B_ρ(ξ)) as δ ↓ 0; since e^{c(ρ)}/ρⁿ > 0, choose δ ∈ (0, r) with e^{c(ρ)}μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/ρⁿ + c(ρ) < ωt. Let |η − ξ| < δ. Then |η − ξ| < r and B_ρ(η) ⊆ B_{ρ+δ}(ξ) (triangle inequality), so a_η(ρ) ≤ μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/ρⁿ (monotonicity of the finite measure μ). By 1(d) for this η (with the data of ξ and ρ ∈ (0, r)): ω·V.density η ≤ e^{c(ρ)}a_η(ρ) + c(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)}μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/ρⁿ + c(ρ) < ωt, hence V.density η < t. Thus V.density < t on the neighbourhood {|η − ξ| < δ} of ξ, in particular on a neighbourhood of ξ relative to U; this is upper semicontinuity of V.density within U at ξ. As ξ ∈ U was arbitrary, V.density is upper semicontinuous on U. ∎

Siblings used: mcm_exp_neg_integral_ftc (FTC), mcm_annulus_integration_by_parts (IBP), mcm_density_usc_of_monotone (DU). Assume (GF) and (UI). Fix n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H, Λ ≥ 0 with V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H and |H(x)| ≤ Λ for μ-a.e. x ∈ U, where μ := μ_V; by (GF), μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K. For a centre ξ write a_ξ(τ) := μ(B_τ(ξ))/τⁿ, e_ξ, w_ξ as in (UI), and D_ξ(s, t) := ∫_{B_t(ξ)∖B_s(ξ)} w_ξ dμ. Note w_ξ ≥ 0 everywhere (q_ξ is a quotient of two squares and |x−ξ|ⁿ ≥ 0), hence D_ξ ≥ 0.
Part A (the identity). Fix ξ, R with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U and write a, e, w, D for a_ξ, e_ξ, w_ξ, D_ξ.
A0. If R ≤ 0, F ≡ 1 and G ≡ 1 work: (0, R) is empty and no σ, ρ satisfy 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R. Assume R > 0.
A1. For τ ∈ (0, R]: B_τ(ξ) ⊆ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U is compact, so μ(B_τ(ξ)) < ∞; for μ-a.e. x ∈ B_τ(ξ) we have x ∈ U, |H(x)| ≤ Λ and |⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ |x−ξ||H(x)| ≤ τΛ. Hence |∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ| ≤ τΛμ(B_τ(ξ)) and |e(τ)| ≤ τΛμ(B_τ(ξ))/τ^{n+1} = Λa(τ).
A2. Let E(τ) := e(τ)/a(τ) (real division, x/0 = 0). For τ ∈ (0, R]: if a(τ) > 0 then |E(τ)| = |e(τ)|/a(τ) ≤ Λ and E(τ)a(τ) = e(τ); if a(τ) = 0 then E(τ) = 0, |E(τ)| ≤ Λ, and A1 gives |e(τ)| ≤ 0, so e(τ) = 0 = E(τ)a(τ). Thus |E| ≤ Λ and e = E·a on (0, R].
A3. E is integrable on (0, R]: τ ↦ μ(B_τ(ξ)) is nondecreasing on ℝ (balls increase and have finite measure), hence Borel, so a is Borel on (0, ∞). For each k ∈ ℕ, (UI) with radii R/(k+1) ≤ R shows that e is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on (R/(k+1), R]; since (0, R] = ⋃_k (R/(k+1), R], e is a.e.-strongly measurable on (0, R]. So E = e/a is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by Λ on (0, R], which has finite Lebesgue measure; hence E is integrable on (0, R].
A4. Define F(ρ) := exp(−∫_{(0,ρ]}E) for all ρ ∈ ℝ. For ρ ∈ (0, R], |∫_{(0,ρ]}E| ≤ Λρ (|E| ≤ Λ on (0, ρ] ⊆ (0, R] and λ((0, ρ]) = ρ), so e^{−Λρ} ≤ F(ρ) ≤ e^{Λρ}; in particular F(ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λρ}, e^{Λρ}] for ρ ∈ (0, R). By FTC with g := E: F'(τ) := −E(τ)F(τ) is integrable on (0, R] and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}F' for all 0 ≤ σ ≤ t ≤ R.
A5. Let 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R. For σ ≤ s ≤ t ≤ ρ we have 0 < s ≤ t and B_t(ξ) ⊆ U, so (UI) gives a(t) − a(s) = D(s, t) + ∫_{(s,t]}e; (UI) with (σ, ρ) gives integrability of e on (σ, ρ] and of w on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ). F' is integrable on (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R] and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}F' for t ∈ [σ, ρ] (A4). IBP applied to (μ, ξ, w ≥ 0, a, e, F, F', σ, ρ) yields that x ↦ F(|x−ξ|)w(x) is μ-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ) and F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = I(σ, ρ) + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}(Fe + F'a), where I(σ, ρ) := ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)}F(|x−ξ|)w(x)dμ.
A6. For τ ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R], F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ) = F(τ)(e(τ) − E(τ)a(τ)) = 0 by A2, so the last integral vanishes and F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = I(σ, ρ).
A7. For x ∈ B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ), |x−ξ| ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R), so by A4 and Λ ≥ 0, e^{−ΛR} ≤ e^{−Λ|x−ξ|} ≤ F(|x−ξ|) ≤ e^{Λ|x−ξ|} ≤ e^{ΛR}. Multiplying by w(x) ≥ 0 and integrating (w and F(|·−ξ|)w are integrable there by A5): e^{−ΛR}D(σ, ρ) ≤ I(σ, ρ) ≤ e^{ΛR}D(σ, ρ). Assume (UI). Fix n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H with V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, ξ, σ, ρ, δ with B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, 0 < σ < ρ and τ^{1−n}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|H|dμ ≤ δ for τ ∈ [σ, ρ], where μ := μ_V. Write a(τ) := μ(B_τ(ξ))/τⁿ, e(τ) := τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩dμ and D := ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)}q_ξ/|x−ξ|ⁿ dμ.
1. (UI) with (σ, ρ) (σ ≤ ρ) shows that e is integrable on (σ, ρ] and a(ρ) − a(σ) = D + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}e; hence a(ρ) − a(σ) − D = ∫_{(σ,ρ]}e.
2. Fix τ ∈ (σ, ρ]. B_τ(ξ) is compact and contained in B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U; since H is locally μ-integrable on U (first part of HasMeanCurvatureIn), H and |H| are μ-integrable on B_τ(ξ). For x ∈ B_τ(ξ), |⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ |x−ξ||H(x)| ≤ τ|H(x)|; so x ↦ ⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩ is integrable on B_τ(ξ) and |∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ| ≤ ∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|⟨x−ξ, H⟩|dμ ≤ τ∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|H|dμ. Therefore |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-n}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|H|dμ = τ^{-1}·(τ^{1−n}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|H|dμ) ≤ δ/τ, using τ^{1−n} = τ·τ^{-n} for τ > 0 and the hypothesis at τ ∈ [σ, ρ].
3. τ ↦ δ/τ is continuous on [σ, ρ] (σ > 0), hence integrable on (σ, ρ], and ∫_{(σ,ρ]}δ/τ dτ = δ(log ρ − log σ) = δ log(ρ/σ).
4. By 1–3, |a(ρ) − a(σ) − D| = |∫_{(σ,ρ]}e| ≤ ∫_{(σ,ρ]}δ/τ dτ = δ log(ρ/σ). ∎
proof_key_steps: (UI) gives a(ρ) − a(σ) − D = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e
Local integrability of H on the compact B_τ(ξ) ⊆ U and |⟨x−ξ, H⟩| ≤ τ|H| give |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-1}·τ^{1−n}∫_{B_τ}|H| ≤ δ/τ

subproblems.title: Hölder bound for the mean-curvature error term (Simon 4.2–4.3 at ε = 0; parent (5.1))
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} finite on compact sets, H: E → E, p ∈ ℝ with p > n, ξ ∈ E, and 0 < τ ≤ R, with H ∈ L^p(μ⌞B_R(ξ)). Let A := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(ξ)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p}. Then |τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩dμ| ≤ (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + τ^{-n}μ(B_τ(ξ))), with real powers and μ(B) the real-valued measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (R τ : ℝ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → (n : ℝ) < p → MemLp H (ENNReal.ofReal p) (μ.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) → 0 < τ → τ ≤ R → |(∫ x in closedBall ξ τ, inner ℝ (x - ξ) (H x) ∂μ) / τ ^ (n + 1)| ≤ (R ^ (p - n) * ∫ x in closedBall ξ R, ‖H x‖ ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) / R * (τ / R) ^ (-(n : ℝ) / p) * (1 + μ.real (closedBall ξ τ) / τ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Write B_t := B_t(ξ), I_R := ∫_{B_R}|H|^p dμ, m := μ(B_τ) (finite, since B_τ is compact) and a := m/τⁿ ≥ 0.
1. p > n ≥ 1 gives p > 1. Let q := p/(p−1) be the conjugate exponent, so 1/p + 1/q = 1 and 1/q = 1 − 1/p ∈ (0, 1).
2. As H ∈ L^p(μ⌞B_R) with 0 < p < ∞, |H|^p is μ-integrable on B_R and I_R ∈ [0, ∞). Since R > 0, A = (R^{p−n})^{1/p}I_R^{1/p} = R^{(p−n)/p}I_R^{1/p}, i.e. I_R^{1/p} = A·R^{n/p−1}.
3. B_τ ⊆ B_R and μ(B_τ) < ∞, so H ∈ L^p(μ⌞B_τ) ⊆ L¹(μ⌞B_τ) (p ≥ 1, finite measure). For x ∈ B_τ, |⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ |x−ξ||H(x)| ≤ τ|H(x)|; hence ⟨x−ξ, H⟩ is μ-integrable on B_τ and |∫_{B_τ}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ| ≤ τ∫_{B_τ}|H|dμ.
4. Hölder's inequality on (B_τ, μ⌞B_τ) with exponents p and q, applied to |H| and the constant function 1 (which lies in L^q because m < ∞): ∫_{B_τ}|H|dμ ≤ (∫_{B_τ}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p}·m^{1/q} ≤ I_R^{1/p}·m^{1−1/p}, using ∫_{B_τ}|H|^p ≤ I_R (nonnegative integrand, B_τ ⊆ B_R).
5. Combining 2–4: |τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ| ≤ τ^{-n}·A·R^{n/p−1}·m^{1−1/p} = A·R^{n/p−1}·τ^{-n}(τⁿa)^{1−1/p} = A·R^{n/p−1}·τ^{−n/p}·a^{1−1/p} = (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}a^{1−1/p} (if m = 0 both sides vanish).
6. For a ≥ 0 and 0 < 1 − 1/p < 1: a^{1−1/p} ≤ 1 when a ≤ 1 and a^{1−1/p} ≤ a when a ≥ 1, so a^{1−1/p} ≤ 1 + a. Since (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p} ≥ 0, we get |τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ| ≤ (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + a) = (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + τ^{-n}μ(B_τ(ξ))). ∎
proof_key_steps: p > 1; conjugate exponent q with 1/q = 1 − 1/p

subproblems.title: Lᵖ mean-curvature monotonicity with corrected κ (Simon 4.2–4.8 for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R; parent Step 5)
subproblems.statement: Assume (GF) and (UI) [as in bounded_curvature]. Then LpMonotonicity holds: for n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H such that V has generalized mean curvature H in U, p > n with H ∈ L^p_loc(U) (H ∈ L^p(μ_V⌞K) for every compact K ⊆ U), ξ, R > 0 with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U, and Λ with (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(ξ)}|H|^p dμ_V)^{1/p} ≤ κΛ, κ = (p−n)/(4p): there are F: ℝ → ℝ and G: ℝ × ℝ → ℝ such that for ρ ∈ (0, R], e^{−(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}} ≤ F(ρ) ≤ e^{(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}} and |F(ρ) − 1| ≤ (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}; for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R, G(σ,ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}] and (F(ρ)ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ(ξ)) + (F(ρ) − 1)) − (F(σ)σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ(ξ)) + (F(σ) − 1)) = G(σ,ρ)∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} q_ξ(x)/|x−ξ|ⁿ dμ_V; and ρ ↦ F(ρ)ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ(ξ)) + (F(ρ) − 1) is nondecreasing on (0, R].
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (σ ρ : ℝ), 0 < n → IsOpen U → V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H → closedBall ξ ρ ⊆ U → 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → IntegrableOn (fun τ ↦ (∫ x in closedBall ξ τ, inner ℝ (x - ξ) (H x) ∂V.weight) / τ ^ (n + 1)) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ V.normalRadialSq ξ x / ‖x - ξ‖ ^ n) (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) V.weight ∧ V.weight.real (closedBall ξ ρ) / ρ ^ n - V.weight.real (closedBall ξ σ) / σ ^ n = ∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ, V.normalRadialSq ξ x / ‖x - ξ‖ ^ n ∂V.weight + ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, (∫ x in closedBall ξ τ, inner ℝ (x - ξ) (H x) ∂V.weight) / τ ^ (n + 1)) → LpMonotonicity
subproblems.natural_proof:
Siblings used: mcm_lp_holder_bound (HB), mcm_exp_neg_integral_ftc (FTC), mcm_annulus_integration_by_parts (IBP). (GF): for every n > 0, ℓ, V, μ_V is finite on compact sets, dim T_xV = n μ_V-a.e., x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable. (UI): for n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H with V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, ξ, and 0 < σ ≤ ρ with B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, e_ξ(τ) := τ^{-(n+1)}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x−ξ, H⟩dμ_V is integrable on (σ, ρ], w_ξ := q_ξ/|x−ξ|ⁿ is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ), and a_ξ(ρ) − a_ξ(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)}w_ξ dμ_V + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}e_ξ, where a_ξ(t) := μ_V(B_t(ξ))/tⁿ.
Assume (GF), (UI). Fix n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H with V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, p > n with H ∈ L^p_loc(U), ξ, R > 0 with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U, and Λ with A := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(ξ)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ κΛ, κ := lpKappa n p = (p−n)/(4p), μ := μ_V. By (GF), μ is finite on compact sets. Write a, e, w for a_ξ, e_ξ, w_ξ (w ≥ 0), D(s, t) := ∫_{B_t(ξ)∖B_s(ξ)}w dμ ≥ 0 and θ := 1 − n/p.
1. Constants. p > n ≥ 1 gives p > 1, κ > 0 and θ ∈ (0, 1). A ≥ 0 (a real power of the nonnegative number R^{p−n}∫|H|^p), so Λ ≥ A/κ ≥ 0. B_R(ξ) is compact and contained in U, so H ∈ L^p(μ⌞B_R(ξ)).
2. (4.2–4.3, Hölder.) For τ ∈ (0, R], HB gives |e(τ)| ≤ (A/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + a(τ)) ≤ k(τ)(1 + a(τ)), where k(τ) := (κΛ/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}, because A ≤ κΛ, (τ/R)^{−n/p} ≥ 0 and 1 + a(τ) ≥ 1.
3. Put F₀(τ) := e(τ)/(1 + a(τ)). For τ ∈ (0, R], 1 + a(τ) ≥ 1, |F₀(τ)| ≤ k(τ) and e(τ) = F₀(τ)(1 + a(τ)).
4. Integrability (4.5). Since −n/p > −1, k is integrable on (0, R], and for ρ ∈ (0, R], ∫_{(0,ρ]}k = (κΛ/R)R^{n/p}∫_0^ρ τ^{−n/p}dτ = (κΛ/R)R^{n/p}ρ^θ/θ = κΛ(p/(p−n))(ρ/R)^θ = (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^θ (here the corrected κ is used: κp/(p−n) = 1/4). τ ↦ μ(B_τ(ξ)) is nondecreasing (finite measures of increasing balls), so a is Borel on (0, ∞); by (UI) with radii R/(k+1) ≤ R, e is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each (R/(k+1), R], so on (0, R] = ⋃_k (R/(k+1), R]. Hence F₀ is a.e.-strongly measurable on (0, R] and dominated by k, so F₀ is integrable on (0, R] and ∫_{(0,ρ]}|F₀| ≤ (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^θ for ρ ∈ (0, R].
5. (4.5.) Define F(ρ) := exp(−∫_{(0,ρ]}F₀) for all ρ. For ρ ∈ (0, R] let s := −∫_{(0,ρ]}F₀; then |s| ≤ (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^θ ≤ (Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ, so e^{−(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ} ≤ F(ρ) = e^s ≤ e^{(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ}. Moreover (ρ/R)^θ ≤ 1, so |s| ≤ Λ/4, and by the mean value theorem |e^s − 1| = |s|e^{ζ} for some ζ between 0 and s, whence |F(ρ) − 1| ≤ e^{|s|}|s| ≤ e^{Λ/4}(Λ/4)(ρ/R)^θ ≤ e^{Λ/2}(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ = (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ(ρ/R)^θ. This is the first conjunct.
6. By FTC with g := F₀: F'(τ) := −F₀(τ)F(τ) is integrable on (0, R] and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}F' for all 0 ≤ σ ≤ t ≤ R.
7. (4.4, 4.7.) Let 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R. For σ ≤ s ≤ t ≤ ρ, 0 < s and B_t(ξ) ⊆ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U, so (UI) gives a(t) − a(s) = D(s, t) + ∫_{(s,t]}e; (UI) with (σ, ρ) gives integrability of e on (σ, ρ] and of w on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ). With step 6 (F' integrable on (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R], F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]}F' on [σ, ρ]), IBP applied to (μ, ξ, w, a, e, F, F', σ, ρ) gives: F(|·−ξ|)w is μ-integrable on B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ) and F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = I(σ, ρ) + ∫_{(σ,ρ]}(Fe + F'a), where I(σ, ρ) := ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)}F(|x−ξ|)w(x)dμ. For τ ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R], by step 3, F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ) = F(τ)F₀(τ)(1 + a(τ)) − F₀(τ)F(τ)a(τ) = F₀(τ)F(τ) = −F'(τ). Hence ∫_{(σ,ρ]}(Fe + F'a) = −∫_{(σ,ρ]}F' = −(F(ρ) − F(σ)) by step 6 at t = ρ, and therefore (F(ρ)a(ρ) + (F(ρ) − 1)) − (F(σ)a(σ) + (F(σ) − 1)) = I(σ, ρ).
8. (G.) For x ∈ B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ), |x−ξ| ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R], and (|x−ξ|/R)^θ ≤ 1, so by step 5 and Λ ≥ 0, e^{−Λ} ≤ e^{−Λ/2} ≤ F(|x−ξ|) ≤ e^{Λ/2} ≤ e^{Λ}. Multiplying by w(x) ≥ 0 and integrating (both integrable by step 7): e^{−Λ}D(σ, ρ) ≤ I(σ, ρ) ≤ e^{Λ}D(σ, ρ). Define G(σ, ρ) := I(σ, ρ)/D(σ, ρ) if D(σ, ρ) ≠ 0 and 1 otherwise. If D(σ, ρ) > 0, G(σ, ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}] and G·D = I; if D(σ, ρ) = 0, then I(σ, ρ) = 0, G(σ, ρ) = 1 ∈ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}] (Λ ≥ 0) and G·D = 0 = I. With step 7 this is the second conjunct (4.7) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R.
9. (4.8.) For 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R the difference in step 7 equals G(σ, ρ)D(σ, ρ) ≥ 0 (G > 0, D ≥ 0), so ρ ↦ F(ρ)a(ρ) + (F(ρ) − 1) is nondecreasing on (0, R]. F and G depend only on the data fixed above, which proves LpMonotonicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: κ > 0 and A ≥ 0 force Λ ≥ 0; θ = 1 − n/p ∈ (0, 1)
HB and A ≤ κΛ: |e(τ)| ≤ (κΛ/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + a(τ)) on (0, R]
F₀ := e/(1 + a) is integrable on (0, R] with ∫_{(0,ρ]}|F₀| ≤ (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^θ (corrected κ)
FTC + IBP with Fe + F'a = F F₀ = −F' give (Fa + F − 1)(ρ) − (Fa + F − 1)(σ) = ∫F(|x−ξ|)w dμ
e^{−Λ}D ≤ ∫F(|x−ξ|)w ≤ e^{Λ}D gives G ∈ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}]; G·D ≥ 0 gives monotonicity on (0, R]

subproblems.title: Existence and upper semicontinuity of the density for Lᵖ mean curvature (Simon 4.9; parent Step 6)
subproblems.statement: Assume (GF) [as in bounded_curvature] and the contract proposition LpMonotonicity. Then LpDensity holds: for n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H such that V has generalized mean curvature H in U, and p > n with H ∈ L^p_loc(U) (H ∈ L^p(μ_V⌞K) for every compact K ⊆ U), V.HasDensityAt ξ (V.density ξ) for every ξ ∈ U and V.density is upper semicontinuous on U.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → LpMonotonicity → LpDensity
subproblems.natural_proof:
Sibling used: mcm_density_usc_of_monotone (DU). Assume (GF) and LpMonotonicity. Fix n > 0, ℓ, V, open U, H with V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, p > n and H ∈ L^p_loc(U); μ := μ_V is finite on compact sets by (GF). Write a_η(ρ) := μ(B_ρ(η))/ρⁿ. We verify the hypothesis of DU for V and U; its conclusion is exactly that of LpDensity.
1. Constants. p > n ≥ 1 gives p > 0, κ := lpKappa n p = (p−n)/(4p) > 0 and θ := 1 − n/p ∈ (0, 1).
2. Let ξ ∈ U. Since U is open, choose R > 0 with B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U (if the open ball of radius ε about ξ lies in U, R := ε/3 works). Put A₀ := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_{2R}(ξ)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≥ 0 and Λ := A₀/κ ≥ 0. Take r := R and c(ρ) := e^{Λ/2}Λ(ρ/R)^θ. Since θ > 0, ρ ↦ (ρ/R)^θ is continuous with value 0 at ρ = 0, so c(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
3. Let |η − ξ| < R. Then B_R(η) ⊆ B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U by the triangle inequality. B_{2R}(ξ) is a compact subset of U, so H ∈ L^p(μ⌞B_{2R}(ξ)) and |H|^p is μ-integrable on B_{2R}(ξ); as |H|^p ≥ 0 and B_R(η) ⊆ B_{2R}(ξ), ∫_{B_R(η)}|H|^p dμ ≤ ∫_{B_{2R}(ξ)}|H|^p dμ. Multiplying by R^{p−n} > 0 and taking the nondecreasing power 1/p > 0 of nonnegative numbers: (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(η)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ A₀ = κΛ.
4. LpMonotonicity applied to (n, ℓ, V, U, H, p, η, R, Λ) (with 0 < n, U open, V.HasMeanCurvatureIn U H, n < p, H ∈ L^p_loc(U), 0 < R, B_R(η) ⊆ U and step 3) gives F_η, G_η such that for ρ ∈ (0, R], e^{−(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ} ≤ F_η(ρ) ≤ e^{(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ} and |F_η(ρ) − 1| ≤ (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ(ρ/R)^θ, and ρ ↦ F_η(ρ)a_η(ρ) + (F_η(ρ) − 1) is nondecreasing on (0, R].
5. Put E_η := F_η − 1. For ρ ∈ (0, R): since Λ ≥ 0, (ρ/R)^θ ≥ 0 and e^{Λ/2} ≥ 1, both (Λ/2)(ρ/R)^θ ≤ c(ρ) and (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ(ρ/R)^θ ≤ c(ρ); hence e^{−c(ρ)} ≤ F_η(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)} and |E_η(ρ)| ≤ c(ρ). Also ρ ↦ F_η(ρ)a_η(ρ) + E_η(ρ) is nondecreasing on (0, R) ⊆ (0, R].
6. Thus for every ξ ∈ U the data r = R, c and, for each |η − ξ| < R, F_η and E_η satisfy the hypothesis of DU. DU gives V.HasDensityAt ξ (V.density ξ) for every ξ ∈ U and the upper semicontinuity of V.density on U, which is LpDensity. ∎
proof_key_steps: For ξ ∈ U pick R with B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U and the uniform Λ := A₀/κ, A₀ = (R^{p−n}∫_{B_{2R}(ξ)}|H|^p)^{1/p}
For |η−ξ| < R: B_R(η) ⊆ U and (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(η)}|H|^p)^{1/p} ≤ κΛ, so LpMonotonicity applies at (η, R, Λ)
F_η and E_η := F_η − 1 satisfy the DU bounds with c(ρ) = e^{Λ/2}Λ(ρ/R)^θ → 0, and F_η·a_η + E_η is nondecreasing on (0, R)
Apply DU
